concept: RangeSlider is Slider with two frosted glass caps in the same ruler groove, setting a low and a high end such as a heating schedule's band or a lamp's warm to cool range; the ruler between the caps is printed in heavier ink and the groove there is lit in the caps' quiet tint, while no part turns orange.

material.recipe: A frosted tinted resin, lit from behind by the value

family_difference: Two caps ride the one groove instead of one, each cap is its own role slider that stops at the other so they never cross, and the ruler ticks between the caps print in full ink and twice the stroke to show the chosen span without filling the groove.

default_to_avoid.pattern: two thumb Material range slider with a coloured filled segment between round thumbs
default_to_avoid.why_not: A saturated brand fill spends the unit's one orange on a secondary control, while P1 keeps it for the rotary and P9 allows only a quiet tint from the value's own range.

references.source: Braun HLD 4 / timer and thermostat dials (Dieter Rams era): two set pins on one scale marking a from and a to
Braun audio 1 compact system (Dieter Rams, 1962): linear faders in a slot with a printed ruler scale
packages/react/src/components/Slider (dial): the ruler fader this family follows

derivation.consequence: faders ride a groove with a ruler scale
derivation.form: Both caps ride Slider's narrow recessed groove under the same printed ruler, with an optional row of numerals below.

derivation.consequence: rotaries and faders settle into the nearest detent
derivation.form: Each cap follows the pointer while dragged and settles into the nearest detent on its own spring of mass 1.4, stiffness 520 and damping 46.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The span between the caps is shown by heavier ruler printing and a quiet glass tint, so the groove, the caps and the span never use action.accent.

derivation.consequence: glass tint comes from the value's own range, warm for warmth, the room's light for a lamp, and stays a quiet tone near the plastic
derivation.form: The tint prop picks the warm, cool or neutral glass range for both caps and the light in the groove between them.

derivation.consequence: a glass part is lit through from behind by the value it holds, and keeps the one top-left light on its surface
derivation.form: The groove between the caps fills with the tint, each frosted cap shows it through itself and keeps the lit hairline and short shadow of the single light.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: Each cap is a role slider in the tab order: arrows step a detent, PageUp and PageDown a larger step, Home and End the ends it may reach.

options.name: inked span: the ruler ticks between the caps print in full ink
ink floor: the groove floor between the caps is lit in grille ink
facing caps: each cap carries its index on the edge facing the other

variants.reason: A keeps Slider's cap and groove unchanged and tells the span by printing, as P5 asks of labels; B is the filled segment of the default in grey ink, and C adds two cap shapes that a person must learn for one control.

mechanism.travel: full track length, each cap stopped by the other

root.why: The fader fills the inline size of its column and keeps at least five touch targets of length in every state.

header.why: The label and the two values sit on one printed line above the track, aligned to its two ends.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the word printed above a fader on a case.

value.why: The low and high values are printed with tabular figures so the digits do not shift while a cap moves.

fader.why: The whole track takes the pointer and stays at least 44px tall, so a press anywhere brings the nearer cap.

rule.why: The ruler band above the groove holds one printed tick per detent, spanning the travel of the caps' centres.

tick.why: Each tick is a hairline of printing, flat on the material with no shadow, so it never reads as a part.

major.why: The ends and the middle of the ruler are printed in the primary ink so the scale can be read at a glance.

inside.why: Ticks between the two caps print in full step ink at twice the stroke, so the span reads by printing and never by orange.

groove.why: Both caps ride the one narrow recessed slot drawn with inverse light; its hairline edge in line.ring holds 3:1 against the body.

thumb.why: Each cap sits in a 44px square hit area that moves with it, so either cap can be grabbed and focused on its own.

cap.why: Each cap is a raised part of frosted glass in the range's tint, showing the groove's light through itself and casting the short part shadow down and to the right of the single light.

fill.why: The groove between the two caps is lit in their tint, a quiet tone near the plastic that marks the chosen band and is never the orange.

scale.why: The optional numeral row under the groove prints the scale values in the smallest type step, as on Slider.

numeral.why: Each numeral is centred under its tick with tabular figures, in medium weight at the smallest size step.

hover.why: Hover darkens a cap's printed index one step and never lifts or grows the cap toward the pointer.

focus-visible.why: The focused cap carries the same dark ring every part shows, so the person knows which end the keys will move.

aria-disabled=true.why: A disabled range loses both caps' height and fades to half, while the groove, ruler and values stay readable.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion each cap jumps to its detent at once and the index ink changes with no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours both caps turn matte with real borders, the band between them becomes Highlight, and the index lines and ticks are drawn in system colours.

data-tint=warm.why: A band of warmth, such as a heating schedule, takes the warm amber glass range for both caps and the light between them.

data-tint=cool.why: A band of coolness, such as a cooling schedule, takes the cool steel glass range for both caps and the light between them.

@media prefers-reduced-transparency: red.why: When the reader asks for less transparency both caps and the band light turn matte in the same tint, so the band still reads at once.

border-color.why: The index ink step on hover comes in over 120ms and goes back over 240ms on the decelerating curve, fast in and slow out.
